title: st attach accepts a repo-relative path, reports ok, and mints a duplicate attachment entry that no verb removes and doctor never reports
body:
**`intent st attach` ACCEPTS A REPO-RELATIVE PATH, RETURNS rc=0 AND `ok:`, AND MINTS A SECOND ATTACHMENT ENTRY FOR A FILE THAT ALREADY HAS ONE.** The duplicate's path resolves nowhere relative to the thread root, no verb removes it, and `intent doctor` does not report it.

**THE GATE'S OWN REMEDY INVITES THE INPUT THAT BREAKS IT.** `canon_commit_check.sh` prints `intent st attach <ST> <rel-path> --from <file>`. *Relative* to a reader means relative to the repo -- it is the path `git status` just printed at them, and it is the path they have in hand at exactly the moment the gate refuses. The verb wants it relative to the THREAD, says so nowhere, and accepts the other form without complaint.

## Reproduction, driven 2026-09-05 in a scratch project, on BOTH builds

    intent st attach ST0001 parity/probe.txt --from intent/st/ST0001/parity/probe.txt
      ok: parity/probe.txt written to ST0001
      canon attachments: ["parity/probe.txt"]

    intent st attach ST0001 intent/st/ST0001/parity/probe.txt --from <same file>
      ok: intent/st/ST0001/parity/probe.txt written to ST0001      <- rc=0
      canon attachments: ["intent/st/ST0001/parity/probe.txt", "parity/probe.txt"]

Identical on v3.0.0 (`80d8b2ca`) and at HEAD (`92e4d914`), so this is not a regression and not post-cut -- it is how the verb has behaved across the cut. **A reader of the published build reaches it through the remedy the tool itself prints.**

## Why it is worse than a duplicate row

**NOTHING REPORTS IT.** `intent doctor` on the probe carrying the duplicate returns one finding, `backup-stale`, and says nothing about the attachment. The verb whose entire job is model inconsistency is silent on a model inconsistency it can see.

**NOTHING REMOVES IT.** `intent st` ships `new start done cancel triage hold resume reopen reinstate hydrate dehydrate list show edit attach sync bootstrap`. There is no detach. Once minted, the row is reachable only by hand-editing the canon JSON and pushing it back with `sync --to-store`, which is `0185`'s workaround for a different missing verb.

**IT IS FOUND, IF AT ALL, BY A GATE THE CONSUMER MAY NOT HAVE.** In this estate `canon_commit_check.sh` refused the commit with *this commit's canon names bytes the commit does not carry* -- correct, and it is the only thing that caught it. A consumer who has not installed the pre-commit hook gets rc=0, `ok:`, and a silently wrong extract.

## How it was found

Filing eleven `AC-02.3` dispositions, I passed `st attach` the repo-relative path because that is the form the remedy reads as. The commit was refused. The verb had reported success.

## What would settle it

Either the verb rejects a path that is not thread-relative -- it can tell, since the offending form starts with the thread's own directory prefix -- or it normalises it. Silently minting a second entry is the one behaviour that should not survive. `intent doctor` should report two attachment rows naming one file regardless.

## Adjacent, and NOT the same

`0199` and `0184` are both about that remedy being INERT -- following it correctly does not clear the gate. This is the opposite failure: following it as written, with the obvious reading of `<rel-path>`, actively corrupts the extract and reports success.


---

**CLOSED 2026-09-05, `ratified_in: "vc, 2026-09-05, under hv's pen granted 2026-08-22"`.** Fixed at `525dd7f7`. The close criterion is the fix being in the tree and DRIVEN; **the shipped pair lagging is a delivery fact rather than a property of this row** (vc's ruling, recorded because the estate had been inconsistent about it: holding a row open until a rebuild reaches the shared pair couples every issue to hv's release hand, and the register would stop meaning *this defect is present*. The pair's lag is already tracked by something that owns it -- the binary names its own source commit and the gate's self-provenance arm reports currency on every commit).

## THE ROW NAMED ONE SHAPE AND THE DOOR WAS ACCEPTING FIVE

**This is the part worth keeping.** Before fixing what this issue describes, the door was probed with eight paths. **Eight were accepted at rc=0 and eight rows were minted**, on `da5919e8`:

| path offered | before |
| --- | --- |
| `design.md` | `ok:` -- correct |
| `parity/probe.txt` | `ok:` -- correct |
| `intent/st/ST0001/parity/probe.txt` | `ok:` -- **this row** |
| `../escape.md` | `ok:` -- climbs out of the thread |
| `/tmp/absolute.md` | `ok:` -- absolute |
| `./dotslash.md` | `ok:` -- second spelling of one file |
| `sub/../normal.md` | `ok:` -- resolves inside and is still a second spelling |
| `` (empty) | `ok:` -- a row naming no file at all |

**Fixing only the shape this issue names would have left four open.** An issue is written about the instance somebody happened to hit; the probe that finds the rest cost one loop.

## The fix: REFUSE, and the radius was measured BEFORE the choice

`intent/st/ST0056/parity/tools/` aside, the check has one home -- `project::attachment_path_fault`, beside `within_attachment_cap`, whose doc already gives the reason: every door that writes an attachment must refuse the same set, and two copies drift into one door refusing what another accepts.

**Refuse rather than normalise**, because normalising silently REINTERPRETS an address instead of correcting the person who wrote it, and because an accepted-and-wrong write is the failure the check exists to stop. **The choice was only mine to make because the radius was counted first**: over this estate's 369 distinct attachment paths, **zero** are refused by the new rule, so it is additive rather than a migration. A refusal that invalidates existing rows is a migration wearing a fix's clothes, and that decision belongs to hv.

Driven as the defect NOT occurring, on a private release build rather than in unit tests alone: same eight paths, same rig -- the two well-formed ones land, six refuse at rc=1, and canon holds exactly the two legitimate rows.

## The fix shipped a fresh instance of `0268`'s class, caught by reading the rendered output

The first build returned prose and rode on `FacadeError::WriteNotAddressable`, so a correct refusal about a mistyped file path printed the remedy *`PUT` json to a caller-assigned id (an AC or an AT)* -- right for a different caller entirely. **`FacadeError::remedy`'s own doc comment forbids exactly this**: _no two variants share a remedy text -- a remedy that fits two different causes is telling the operator to guess which one they hit_ (AC-04.4). That comment was read while adding the arm underneath it. **A stated rule is not a check**, and the repair is to move the constraint out of prose and into the type: the fault is a `PathFault` KIND with a remedy per cause.

## And the remedy string this issue is about was wrong in a SECOND word

`canon_commit_check.sh` said `intent st attach <ST> <rel-path> --from <file>`. That line's own comment already records it being **one word wrong** and fixed (`0184`: `sync` was named as the writer and is not). `<rel-path>` is the second: *relative* to a reader means relative to the REPOSITORY. It now reads `<path-inside-the-thread>`, matching the verb's own refusal.

**Two separate tokens of one remedy, each wrong, each found by a node following it.** Remedy text is shipped surface that nothing tests -- which is `0263`'s subject from the other side.
